title: A foster or relative caregiver borrowing for a child without exposing a custody case
moment: An aunt who holds court-appointed guardianship (監護) of her nephew after a family crisis comes to a library to get him a children's card. Showing a court order or the household register would expose the custody dispute, the parents' situation and the child's history to a counter clerk and into a scanned record. The library only needs to know that she is a legal guardian of a child under the age limit.
verifier: Public library branch counter and its card registration system
predicate: The holder is the legally appointed guardian of a child under the card's age limit, whatever the legal basis (parent, court-appointed guardian, or foster placement).
disclosed_today: Court order or household register pages showing parents' names, reasons for guardianship, addresses and the child's full record, often photocopied.
issuer: The family court (家事法庭) for court-appointed guardianship, or the local social affairs bureau (社會局) for foster placements, countersigned into a wallet credential through the household registration office
why_zk: Here the verifier collects far more than it needs, and the extra material is sensitive and stigmatizing. A signed guardianship credential that proves only membership in the 'legal guardian of a minor' set hides the basis and the parents' details, in the same way a privileged consultation should not expose the matter to outsiders. Weakness: courts and social bureaus do not currently issue digital credentials, so this would need new issuer pipelines, and the number of such cases per library is small, so the justification is humane rather than statistical.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In attorney-client privilege, a sensitive matter is shared with an advisor without outsiders learning more than needed; here, the custody case behind the guardianship stays with the court and the library clerk learns only that the holder is a guardian.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A party must consult an advisor about a sensitive matter without the advisor, or anyone else, learning or revealing more than the matter requires, but the protection breaks as soon as an outsider is in the room unless the outsider is essential to the relationship. | mechanism: Evidentiary privilege over communications, lost by third-party presence except essential agents such as interpreters; no technical mechanism.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In the EUDI wallet recital, a relying party gets only the attribute it needs from a larger attestation; here, the single guardian-of-a-minor attribute is drawn out of the court order or foster placement record.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A verifier needs one attribute from a larger identity record, but the holder cannot share just that attribute from the record. | mechanism: Selective disclosure of attributes from electronic attestations held in the EU Digital Identity Wallet.

title: Daily gate check by the market inspector without a roster of permit holders
moment: Each evening a committee patrol officer walks the stall rows at a night market and checks that every vendor setting up has a current permit, today by reading the laminated permit card and noting names and permit numbers in a notebook that gets typed into a shared spreadsheet.
verifier: Committee patrol officer doing evening setup inspection
predicate: Vendor's food-hygiene and stall permit is current as of today, shown as a fresh presentation tied to this evening and this market
disclosed_today: Name, permit number, photo, registered address and food categories read off the card and copied into a spreadsheet kept by the committee
issuer: Local health bureau, issuing the permit credential to the vendor's phone wallet with an expiry and revocation status
why_zk: The officer needs a yes/no for tonight, not a durable log of who sells what and where they live. A presentation bound to the date and market lets the check pass without creating a spreadsheet that can be leaked or used to track vendors across markets. Weakness: the committee may have a regulatory or lease-management reason to record which permit holder occupies which stall, and many older vendors do not use smartphone wallets.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In the ALA library-records policy, the library avoids keeping a readable log of who borrowed what; here, the patrol officer's nightly check plays that role by recording only a pass/fail tick rather than a roster of identified vendors.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A service provider must keep a record of who used what without that record becoming a readable log of a person's interests, but the duty is a recommended policy that depends on each institution adopting it and on courts or subpoenas being resisted. | mechanism: Institutional confidentiality policy plus procedures for handling subpoenas and law-enforcement requests; no technical minimization of records is specified.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In SameSite cookies, a credential is sent only to the issuing context so unrelated observers cannot match the holder across sites; here, the permit presentation is scoped to this one market and date so that two different markets cannot link the same vendor.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A stored credential should be presented only to the party that issued it in the current context, but the browser sends it on any request the context triggers, so an unrelated observer can match the holder across contexts. | mechanism: The SameSite cookie attribute, which limits the cookie to same-site requests (Strict, Lax, or None); the IETF draft describes it as a per-cookie setting, and cross-site behaviour depends on the chosen value.

title: Carpool app driver check for a weekly Hsinchu science-park commute
moment: A software engineer joins a new weekday carpool from Taichung to Hsinchu Science Park. The group organiser asks each rider to post a selfie with ID and a screenshot of a police record, so the driver and three riders can feel safe sharing a car at 7am. The organiser keeps all of it in a shared Google Drive folder.
verifier: The carpool organiser (a peer) and the fellow riders, via the carpool app
predicate: Rider is not on the violent-offender list, shown once per group join, with a per-group pseudonym so the same person cannot be linked across different carpool groups
disclosed_today: Selfie with ID, full name, ID number, and a record screenshot, uploaded to a shared drive visible to all members
issuer: The carpool platform (e.g., a ride-sharing company) acting as a relying issuer after it checks the person once against the police service, then signing a reusable non-membership credential
why_zk: The riders need to trust a stranger for a short drive, not hold a dossier on them; a per-context proof avoids a shared folder that links a rider's real identity across groups. Weakness: if the platform is the issuer, riders rely on the platform's one-time check, and the credential does not prove anything about behaviour after issuance; unlinkability across groups also hides repeat complaints.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In an-a-samesite-cookies, a SameSite attribute stops a cookie being sent in cross-site requests so third parties cannot recognise the holder across sites; here, a per-group presentation pseudonym plays that role so one carpool group cannot match the rider to other groups.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A stored credential should be presented only to the party that issued it in the current context, but the browser sends it on any request the context triggers, so an unrelated observer can match the holder across contexts. | mechanism: The SameSite cookie attribute, which limits the cookie to same-site requests (Strict, Lax, or None); the IETF draft describes it as a per-cookie setting, and cross-site behaviour depends on the chosen value.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In an-b-attorney-client, confidentiality breaks when an outsider is present unless essential to the relationship; here, the organiser's shared drive plays the outsider whose presence leaks the record, and the zero-knowledge presentation removes the need for any third party to see the underlying record.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A party must consult an advisor about a sensitive matter without the advisor, or anyone else, learning or revealing more than the matter requires, but the protection breaks as soon as an outsider is in the room unless the outsider is essential to the relationship. | mechanism: Evidentiary privilege over communications, lost by third-party presence except essential agents such as interpreters; no technical mechanism.

title: Weekend children's calligraphy class volunteer teacher
moment: A Taipei temple runs a free Saturday calligraphy and Chinese-chess class for neighbourhood primary-school children. A retired teacher offers to help. Today the temple secretary photocopies her ID card and asks for a 良民證 (police criminal record certificate), which lists any record in full and is then kept in a drawer.
verifier: The temple's administrative committee (管理委員會) running the children's programme
predicate: Holder is not on the register of persons with child-related offence or fraud convictions (non-membership), valid for this month.
disclosed_today: Full name, ID number, address, photo and the whole criminal record certificate, including unrelated old minor entries, as a paper copy kept indefinitely.
issuer: The Ministry of Justice or the National Police Agency, which already issues the 良民證 and could sign a narrow 'no listed conviction' claim.
why_zk: Moderate. The need is a yes/no on a list, while a paper certificate leaks the whole record and the ID number, which is the permanent identifier that cannot be changed after a leak. A non-membership proof against a signed register lets the temple learn only that the volunteer is not listed. It is weak where the law already requires or allows the temple to see the full record, and where freshness depends on how often the register is updated. A leaked copy of a certificate can also be reused.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In the 2025 ID-number misuse case, the unchangeable ID number copied from a card keeps being presented by others; here, the photocopied ID and certificate in the temple drawer play that role, and a proof that never reveals the number removes the copy that could be misused.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: Once the number that identifies a person leaks, reissuing the physical card does not stop someone presenting the same number, so verifiers that check the number and a photo can be fooled. | mechanism: None; reissuing the card does not change the number.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In GDPR data minimisation, a controller should take only what the purpose needs but has no way to ask for less than a whole document; here, the 'not on the list' proof plays the narrower field in place of the full certificate.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A rule obliges anyone requesting information to take only what the purpose needs, but gives no practical way to request less than a whole document. | mechanism: Legal principle of data minimisation; no technical mechanism specified.

title: University scholarship desk checks status without seeing household registry
moment: A first-year student from Hualien applies for the indigenous student tuition-support scholarship at the university's student affairs office. Staff currently ask for a full household registration transcript (戶籍謄本) and photocopy it, which shows parents, address, birthplace and marital history, when the only question is whether the applicant holds recognised indigenous status.
predicate: Holder is currently registered with recognised indigenous status (any of the recognised peoples), valid on the application date
disclosed_today: Full household registration transcript or indigenous identity card photocopy: name, national ID number, address, family members, tribe, tribal name, birth details
issuer: Ministry of Interior household registration offices (戶政事務所), with the Council of Indigenous Peoples as the authority for status rules
why_zk: Strong fit: the fact is already a government registry entry, so an issuer exists and the claim is a simple membership proof. The office needs a yes/no, not the family tree. Weakness: the scholarship may legitimately need the specific people (e.g. Amis vs Atayal) for quota or reporting, in which case a selective-disclosure credential should reveal that one attribute only. Also, institutions may keep copies for audit, so the benefit depends on accepting a verifiable presentation as the audit record.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In gdpr-data-minimisation, a controller collects a whole document when a narrower field would serve the purpose; here, the household transcript plays the whole document and the single 'recognised indigenous status' flag plays the narrower field.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A rule obliges anyone requesting information to take only what the purpose needs, but gives no practical way to request less than a whole document. | mechanism: Legal principle of data minimisation; no technical mechanism specified.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In an-b-census-title13, the agency may publish only aggregates from which no individual can be singled out; here, the university's scholarship report to the Ministry of Education plays the publication and receives only counts of verified recipients per people, never individual records.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: An agency holding individual responses must release aggregate results, and the legal duty bars any output from which a particular respondent can be singled out, while the holder's staff can still see the raw records. | mechanism: Statutory use limitation and publication prohibition enforced by sworn-oath duties and penalties; statistical disclosure limitation (for example differential privacy in later census products) is a technical layer not specified in the statute.

title: Temple lodging and meal booking for a congregation retreat at a mountain guesthouse
moment: A congregation of a Taiwanese folk-religion temple books a night at a mountain guesthouse near Alishan that gives a pilgrim group rate and a vegetarian meal package. The guesthouse owner, to confirm the group really is the temple's, asks the leader to send a photo of the roster, each person's believer card and the ID card front and back via LINE, then keeps the photos on a phone.
verifier: Guesthouse owner granting the pilgrim group rate
predicate: Each guest is a member of the named congregation (membership only), checked at check-in in person.
disclosed_today: Photos of ID cards, believer cards and the full roster with names, sent through a messaging app and retained on the owner's phone.
issuer: The temple's committee issuing the credential; as a fallback, the tour leader (a peer) co-signs a group-attendance token.
why_zk: At check-in the owner only needs to see a valid membership presentation on the guest's phone, in the manner of inspecting an original card and keeping nothing, with no photo copy needed. A wallet check done at the desk and leaving no stored copy replaces the LINE photo trail that is the real privacy loss. Weakness: this is a small, trust-based business and the owner has little incentive to adopt a wallet verifier, and for lodging registration the owner still has a legal duty to record identity, so the proof only replaces the religion-related photos.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In the household register rule, the applicant shows the original document for inspection and the agency states no copy requirement; here, the guest's wallet presentation at the guesthouse desk plays the original document, shown once and not photographed.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A person asking an agency for a record must prove identity; the rule specifies inspecting the original card rather than handing over a copy, and it does not say the agency retains anything. | mechanism: Original identity document shown for in-person inspection; the checklist states no retention or copy requirement.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In sealed-bid rules, submissions stay in a restricted-access box and are only opened by a designated official to identify them; here, the tour leader's roster plays the sealed bid, held in the wallet and opened only by the owner's verifier app for the single check-in purpose.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A party submits a value that must stay hidden from competitors until a fixed moment, while the holder of the submissions must be able to prove later that none were seen early and must handle identifying wrappers without exposing the content. | mechanism: Physical and access-control safeguarding of sealed bids with designated-official exception for envelope identification, plus a written record of any mistaken early opening.

title: Landlord accepts early lease termination without seeing the protection order
moment: A tenant in Taichung who holds a civil protection order against a violent ex-partner needs to leave her rental mid-term. Today she hands the landlord the court's 通常保護令 copy to waive the early-termination penalty, and the landlord sees the abuser's name, the allegations, the court and the case details, and may keep a photocopy.
verifier: Private landlord or property-management agency handling an early lease termination
predicate: Holder is covered by a protection order that is active today and whose validity window overlaps the requested lease-break date
disclosed_today: Full protection order document: abuser's name, case number, court, findings, children's names, the holder's old address, sometimes a photocopy retained in the tenant file
issuer: Court that issued the order (judicial registry), possibly via the 家庭暴力暨性侵害防治中心 attestation channel
why_zk: A time-bounded predicate (active now, covers the break window) is exactly what the landlord needs; the abuser's identity and case content are irrelevant to the lease decision. Weakness: it only helps if landlords agree to accept the proof in place of the paper order, and few small landlords have verifier software, so it needs a simple QR or app flow or a social-worker intermediary.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In the EUDI wallet, selective disclosure releases only the one attribute a relying party needs from a larger attestation; here, the court-issued protection order plays the larger record and 'active and covers the break window' plays the single attribute.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A verifier needs one attribute from a larger identity record, but the holder cannot share just that attribute from the record. | mechanism: Selective disclosure of attributes from electronic attestations held in the EU Digital Identity Wallet.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In attorney-client privilege, confidentiality collapses when an unnecessary third party is in the room; here, the landlord plays the outsider who should not be handed the case details, so the proof must be a narrow yes or no.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A party must consult an advisor about a sensitive matter without the advisor, or anyone else, learning or revealing more than the matter requires, but the protection breaks as soon as an outsider is in the room unless the outsider is essential to the relationship. | mechanism: Evidentiary privilege over communications, lost by third-party presence except essential agents such as interpreters; no technical mechanism.

title: Group travel insurance quote for a temple incense-tour with affiliation kept out of the policy file
moment: A temple tour group of 40 people goes on a 3-day incense-offering trip to Mount Wutai-style sister temples abroad or around the island. The agent wants a group policy and the insurer's broker asks for a roster stating which congregation each traveller belongs to, to apply the group rate. The roster, with religion implied, goes by email to the broker and sits in the insurer's underwriting system.
verifier: Insurance broker underwriting a group travel policy
predicate: Traveller belongs to the named congregation that qualifies for the group rate (membership only, no religion field).
disclosed_today: Name, ID number, birth date and the congregation name, which reveals religion, for every traveller.
issuer: The congregation or temple association signing a membership credential; the broker's insurer accepts it as the 'affinity group' proof.
why_zk: The group rate is an affinity-group discount, so the broker needs a membership proof, not a roster naming the faith. A selective-disclosure presentation lets the traveller prove the affinity discount and disclose the legally required insurance fields (name, ID, birth date) separately, so the religion link is not stored in the policy file. The broker can also ask for the minimum scope and the wallet shows what is released. Weakness: the insurer may still require the group name on the policy, which exposes the affinity anyway, and the broker can request a broader presentation than needed.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In OAuth, the client requests a narrow scope but the server may grant more or less than requested; here, the broker's request for the 'group-rate membership' predicate plays the scope request, and the wallet grants only the membership proof rather than the full congregation record.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A holder asks a verifier for a credential covering more attributes than the single fact the relying party needs, and the issuer has no obligation to honour a narrower request. | mechanism: The client states a scope parameter in the request, and the authorization server returns the granted scope in the token response; the server may grant less than requested.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In the TW Digital Identity Wallet, the user picks which fields to disclose after scanning a QR code; here, the traveller picks at the broker's counter to release the membership predicate and the legally required identity fields as separate disclosures.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A user must prove one eligibility fact to a counter, while the credential holds a whole identity record and the user chooses fields at presentation time with no field-level guarantee. | mechanism: Per-scenario field selection after scanning a QR code, confirmed by biometric check, in the TW DIW sandbox.
